title: Reverse Each Word
lesson:
## Strings

Strings are sequences of characters enclosed in quotes.

```python
greeting = "Hello, World!"
name = 'Alice'
```

### Common string methods
| Method | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `.upper()` | Uppercase | `"hello".upper()` → `"HELLO"` |
| `.lower()` | Lowercase | `"HELLO".lower()` → `"hello"` |
| `.strip()` | Remove whitespace | `"  hi  ".strip()` → `"hi"` |
| `.replace(a, b)` | Replace substring | `"cat".replace("c","b")` → `"bat"` |
| `.split(sep)` | Split into list | `"a,b".split(",")` → `["a","b"]` |
| `.join(lst)` | Join list | `"-".join(["a","b"])` → `"a-b"` |
| `.count(sub)` | Count occurrences | `"abca".count("a")` → `2` |
| `.find(sub)` | Find index | `"hello".find("l")` → `2` |

### Slicing
Access parts of a string with `[start:end:step]`:

```python
s = "Python"
print(s[0:3])   # Pyt
print(s[::-1])  # nohtyP  (reversed)
print(s[2:])    # thon
```

### f-strings
```python
name = "World"
print(f"Hello, {name}!")  # Hello, World!
```

### String multiplication
```python
print("ha" * 3)  # hahaha
```
description:
Given the string `"hello world python"`, reverse each individual word (not the whole string) and print the result. The word order stays the same.

**Expected output:**
```
olleh dlrow nohtyp
```
